claim: When a device or media handle is acquired asynchronously (a camera or mic grant behind a permission prompt), give the effect that asked a liveness flag and stop a handle that arrives after it was released, because the consumer can let go while the prompt is open and the late grant is otherwise kept with nobody to reap it.
because: phone camera effect: a grant landing after the panel changed became the active camera; red then green. media-resource-lifecycle covers reap-on-replace and unmount but not the in-flight acquisition race.

claim: When a test claims work runs concurrently, assert how many units were in flight at once (or release the stubs only when all have started), never an elapsed-time upper bound, because a loaded runner stretches every timer and turns a concurrency claim into a race against the machine.
because: a parallel-health suite case (<120 ms over four 40 ms stubs) failed 52 of 64 runs under parallel load; an in-flight count failed 0 of 64 and still caught a deliberately serial version (peak 1).

claim: When commands (not state) cross from I/O threads into a UI loop, carry them on a queue, not a latest-value holder, because a latest-value holder silently drops every command of a burst but the last.
because: undo/redo/seek were sent through a latest-value flow read by recomposition; a test showed 1 of 3 back-to-back commands delivered, and a channel fixed it to 3 of 3.

claim: When a gate starts a tool through the package manager's shim directory (node_modules/.bin and the like) and the install may be a link to another checkout, start the tool by its package file instead, because the shims are not part of the linked packages and an 'is it installed' check over the packages passes while the shim lookup fails.
because: in every worktree the preflight checked the compiler's package through a junction and passed, then the gate failed with 'not recognized' because the donor install had no shim directory; starting the compiler by its file took the typecheck gate from exit 1 to exit 0 with no write to the donor.

claim: When focus is model-driven (a D-pad or remote moves a state index and the element only carries a data-focused or CSS ring, while DOM focus stays on one container), have the view-model produce the spoken line for the lit stop and render it in one polite, atomic live region per surface, because the focus ring never reaches the accessibility tree and nothing else tells a screen reader what Select will open.
because: the TV landing had DOM focus parked on the stage (tabIndex=0) and its lit stop only in data-focused/data-lit; adding view.say in an aria-live region made the region's text follow data-lit in a real browser (phone -> Essay Master -> Linga), with the repo's live check (type floor, safe zone) still green.

claim: When generated text switches to a locale's number format (decimal comma, spaced percent), any check that scans that text for digits must scan the locale-neutral print, because separators split numbers into fragments that match as false hits and silently drop valid items.
because: friend MB-B4: the answer-leak check read '0,99' and '63 %' as leaking 99/63 and discarded most Czech conversion items until it read the plain print; a full-set-of-6 test across systems now pins it.

claim: When a new status mostly behaves like an existing stored one, derive it from stored data at read time and move every rendering site to tables keyed by the full status set, because ternary chains over a string union compile while sending a new member down the last branch.
because: friend MB-B1: 'skipped' derived from unsure+blank (no migration, old records render); a fourth stored verdict would have been ringed as wrong by draw chains TypeScript could not catch.

claim: When a gate borrows a dependency install from another checkout (a link to a donor node_modules), take donors only from the version-control system's own worktree list or an explicit variable, never from a directory crawl up the tree, because the donor's code runs inside the gate and crawled parents include directories every local user can write (shared profile folders, the drive root, /tmp).
because: a worktree preflight crawled 3 parent levels and on a real machine reached C:\Users\Public (interactive users: modify) and 37 drive-root folders (authenticated users may create folders); restricting to git worktree list cut the default to 11 candidates, all worktrees of the repo, with the suite green.

claim: When deciding whether a failure is retryable, classify by cause at every throw site of a class, not by who worded it: an app's own 'refusal' wrapper often wraps a model result (an empty read) that another run can change.
because: architect 2026-10-15 first marked the desk's own refusal class non-retryable; all three throw sites were empty model results and an existing test (zero-item read, retry accepted) went red; fixed by classifying the class retryable.

claim: When a caller judges a model answer in code and asks again, have the seam hand back a ticket (deadline end + next try number) on the answer and accept it on the re-ask, because only the seam knows the provider-specific deadline floor and the attempt count the ledger must show.
because: Two caller re-asks in a study-desk app each took a fresh deadline and were booked as try 1; passing the first answer ticket bounded the turn to one deadline (re-ask test: 320 ms old vs inside 200 ms) and booked try 2.

claim: When moving hand-built prompts onto an assembler, gate it with a static walk that flags any model call whose request names system or prompt itself (or spreads a builder in a file that does not import the assembler), pinned as a shrink-only ratchet, and fingerprint only the authored parts and data labels, never data values, so the ledger groups calls by prompt version without carrying learner text.
because: A desk with 21 hand-assembled call sites moved 11 onto one assembler in a session; the AST walk caught a builder spread a naive walk read as assembled, and the fingerprint stayed stable across learners while moving on every wording change.

claim: When a model's correction of a learner is stored as a whole corrected sentence, judge later recurrence and reuse in code on the token-diff n-grams (the changed words plus a neighbour, guarded to contain a content word), not on the whole sentence, because a whole corrected sentence is almost never said again verbatim and the loop never closes.
because: firetv Linga: 0 of 11 taught fix sentences recurred verbatim in 569 stored learner answers and 'It came back' fired 0 times in every stored run; an LCS slip/fix key caught all 6 known recurrences plus 1 more over 149 lines with 0 false cross-learner flags (2 cross-learner hits were real slips)

claim: When a deterministic answer checker accepts several written forms of one value, decide per answer kind which forms are legitimate (percent, fraction, decimal) in one table keyed by every kind, because a kind missing from a hand-kept 'amount' list silently marks 2400% right for 24 kg.
because: maths-school optimize 2026-10-21: three of nineteen kinds were missing from check()'s amount lists; 5 of 9 percent writings were judged right or wrong; fixed in 6acd2750 and pinned by a table test

claim: When a cross-platform launcher starts a Windows batch wrapper through cmd, name it by its quoted absolute path, because with NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath set (agent harnesses set it) cmd does not search the current directory and a bare name is 'not recognized'.
because: firetv tools/gradlew.cjs exited 1 before Gradle started for every agent; the absolute path fixed it, pinned by a stub-wrapper test

claim: When a Windows PowerShell 5.1 script runs a native command with 2>&1, scope ErrorActionPreference to Continue around that call, because under Stop the first stderr line is a terminating NativeCommandError that ends the script mid-run and loses the child's output and exit code.
because: firetv scripts/model-drift.ps1 died on the first engine warning; reproduced in a 5.1 probe and pinned by a stub-run test

claim: When a user reviews a capped selection (top N) before it is exported, derive the review list from the export's own post-exclusion selection plus the excluded items, because a review list cut before exclusion silently promotes the N+1th item into the export the moment the user excludes one.
because: Study Desk's Twin Card: the review list showed the newest 5 before exclusion while the export took 5 after it; leaving one out exported a 6th unreviewed text. Reproduced red in a route test (1 of 5 unreviewed), fixed by deriving both from one function (0 of 5).

claim: When a runner test proves a timeout or parallelism by timing, read the claim from each fixture's own start/end clock and give innocent sibling fixtures a deterministic start above the observed loaded start, because a list-wide bound or a wall-time ratio turns red on a busy machine with no defect.
because: harness-rules-test went red under four agents (a green sibling took 1705 ms against a 1500 ms list-wide bound); a wall-ratio --jobs assertion measured 7181 vs 9596 ms and could not separate the two arms; fixture-clock overlap and a 2 s / 8 s bound are red-then-green deterministically.

claim: When a detector carries an exemption list keyed by a name or label, test that every exemption still matches something the system produces, because a stale exemption silently pre-excuses a future defect that reuses the name.
because: uat's stray detector excused 5 control labels that a UI redesign had removed; its only test checked the mark against the list it was read from; a coverage guard went red on 5 of 5

claim: When a best-effort ledger rotates its file inline before appending a row, isolate the rotation's failure from the append, because a persistent rename failure (a file held open by a reader) otherwise drops every later row while a once-per-reason log says it only once.
because: firetv engines/meter.ts: a non-replaceable rotation target booked 0 of 3 calls before the fix, 3 of 3 after (econ case g2)

claim: When every state change persists the whole state and one producer is a periodic clock, throttle persistence for that producer's events alone (write at most once per window, and at once on a phase change, a failed last write, or any other event), because the clock otherwise multiplies the whole state's size by its rate while bounding the loss to one window costs nothing else.
because: firetv desk: a 1 Hz timer tick rewrote session.json (up to 3.2 MB of page photos) 60 times a minute; throttled to 2 a minute with a gate pinning that the next non-tick event and a phase turn write at once (2d7de0a6).

claim: When a sans-IO state machine emits several effects for one input and a downstream reducer gates one of them on state another one changes, emit the state-releasing effect first, because the shell applies effects in list order and the gated one is otherwise silently swallowed.
because: pen-core a14a91db: a relay refusal emitted before its Unpaired was hidden by the 'no refusal over a paired pen' rule, so the TV showed a network blink instead of 'wrong PIN'; reordering fixed it (test red then green).

claim: When a test fixture is merged over a recorded default answer set, validate every fixture key against the default's key space and refuse unknown keys, because an unknown key is laid over nothing and the run scores the default, passing while claiming to test the fixture.
because: lab-bench passed exit 0 for 5/5 typo'd or out-of-corpus fixtures (section, problem, page, query, stage); after refusing unknown keys, 5/5 exit 2 and runBench throws (69dcf479)

claim: When a pairing listener reads framed messages before any credential is checked, cap the frame size at the largest legitimate pre-trust message, because common WebSocket servers default to an unbounded frame and one frame then becomes a heap-exhaustion lever against a small device.
because: tv-app's Ktor pen server used maxFrameSize Long.MAX_VALUE; a JVM test showed a 1 MiB frame read whole before the PIN gate, and a 64 KiB cap drops it unread while a 2,000-char message still reads (3b5fde92).

claim: When a web app must be driven by a TV remote on Fire TV, ship it inside a thin WebView wrapper whose activity forwards each remote key to the page as a named keyboard event from a small unit-tested table, because the Silk browser keeps the D-pad, Select, Back and Menu and passes only Play/Pause to a page.
because: Study Desk on a Fire TV Stick 4K (Fire OS 8): Silk delivered only keyCode 179; the stick-app WebView wrapper passed all 24 rows of the remote-key table (friction-log FL-1, STICK-APK-WALK 2026-10-20).

claim: When a native wrapper hands a key to an embedded web page, read the page's defaultPrevented back and leave the app only when the page did not take Back (or on a long press of Back), because otherwise Back either traps the user or exits mid-flow.
because: stick-app key bridge: short Back went to the page, held Back left the app; walked on the stick 2026-10-20 (STICK-APK-WALK lines 26,150).

claim: When keys reach a TV page as synthetic keydown events, build every remote-reachable screen on model-driven focus (arrows move a state index, Enter presses) instead of DOM focus, because a synthetic key moves no browser focus and plain form pages stay unreachable.
because: Study Desk stick walk 2026-10-21: plain form pages could not be reached with injected keys (STICK-DEADLINE-WALK line 68).

claim: When animating web content in a Fire TV WebView, never put a CSS filter or drop-shadow on a will-change or composited layer and bake shadows into the artwork instead, because each such layer re-blurs offscreen every frame and eats the whole frame budget.
because: Study Desk landing idle went from 8.7 fps to 59 fps after moving shadows into the SVG drawing, look within 45-46 dB PSNR (friction-log FL-8).

claim: When a transition mounts large SVG or composited layers on a weak GPU, paint a cheap backdrop of the arriving scene under them, because the compositor runs the animation on time and fills unrastered tiles with whatever lies beneath.
because: Study Desk: a 450-600 ms bare cream (reads white) frame on every module move on the stick disappeared with a sky-gradient backdrop (friction-log FL-7, STICK-WHITE-FRAME 2026-10-20).

claim: When fitting a fixed 1920x1080 web stage to a smaller TV viewport, use CSS zoom (or cap device pixels per stage pixel) rather than transform scale() on composited content, because layers raster at contents scale 1 or more and a scale(.5) stage rasters four times its pixels and overruns the WebView tile budget.
because: Study Desk on the stick: landing tiles 107 MB at rest against an 80/160 MB WebView budget; zoom cut it to 71 MB and removed a second 0.6-0.8 s freeze (friction-log FL-10).

claim: When large static scenery stalls every move on a weak device, draw it once per page load into a canvas so it composites as a texture, because it removes the tile raster from each move at a known GPU-memory cost.
because: Study Desk: longest frame gap of a lamp move fell from 641-669 ms to 271-283 ms, Back from 500-572 to 228-378 ms, for about 46 MB more GPU memory (STICK-PERFORMANCE 2026-10-21).

claim: When an idle TV screen has looping CSS animations, let them run a few loops and rest (or drive them from one low-rate shared clock), because any running animation forces a full redraw every vsync on the device even with steps().
because: Study Desk Math screens redrew 245 frames in 4 s idle on Get ready; after resting the loops idle measured 0 frames (wave 3, 2026-10-23; STICK-PERFORMANCE 2026-10-22).

claim: When UI inside a large layer changes on every remote move, animate only transform and opacity on promoted parts and switch shadow, filter and colour instantly, because a colour or shadow transition re-rasters the whole layer.
because: Study Desk stick: per-move cost fell from about 590 ms to 320 ms (STICK-PERFORMANCE 2026-10-22 lines 23-37).

claim: When a per-frame script needs CSS animation state, keep the values it set at sync time instead of reading Animation.playState or currentTime back, because each read forces a style flush.
because: Study Desk stick traces: about 25 ms per tick spent in forced style recalcs from playState reads (STICK-PERFORMANCE 2026-10-22 line 65).

claim: When judging WebView smoothness on Android or Fire OS, count DrawFn_DrawGL on the RenderThread in a trace window after each key instead of trusting gfxinfo's janky percentage, because gfxinfo times the draw functor against its own deadline.
because: Study Desk Math home ran at a true 60 fps while gfxinfo reported 43 percent janky (friction-log FL-9).

claim: When comparing before and after screenshots of an animated web UI, pause every animation through document.getAnimations() (finite ones at their end, endless at their start) before capture, because a CSS play-state freeze does not reproduce the same frame.
because: Study Desk look checks: capture-to-capture PSNR reached infinity or 88-99 dB only after getAnimations pausing (STICK-PERFORMANCE 2026-10-21 line 188).

claim: When a performance budget targets a weak device, measure only on that device and gate against a ratchet set from the accepted on-device soak plus a tolerance, never the aspiration and never a desktop run, because a target gate is always red and desktop GPUs hide every cost.
because: firetv decision 0020 (stick frame budget as ratchet); every Study Desk raster cost was invisible in desktop Chrome and found only on the stick.

claim: When reading frame pacing from SurfaceFlinger on a TV stick, treat its VSYNC-app jitter as a floor and its present times as a model grid, because a p95 interval bar of 16.7 ms is unreachable even with every frame on time.
because: Death Ride p17 on Fire TV Stick 4K: VSYNC-app tick p95 16.736 ms with no missed frames.

claim: When a performance probe serves stats from the process under test, measure the probe's own allocation first, because the probe can be the churn it reports.
because: Death Ride p13f: the game's GC churn was the probe's own /stats endpoint, 1.378 MB per read.

claim: When an Android TV app plays any sound, price the open audio output stream itself before the mix, because one silent AudioTrack can cost the stick's audio path as much as the full mix and no MMAP route is granted.
because: Death Ride p14/p15 soak on Fire TV Stick 4K.

claim: When a TV app needs a one-time secret, deliver it over the operator's own channel (an adb intent carrying the link the server prints), keep it in memory only, and remember an address only after a server answered there and never a loopback address, because D-pad typing is error-prone and LAN hand-outs let any client claim it.
because: stick-app linking via one adb am start with the desk TV link (friction-log FL-6, STICK-APK-WALK lines 40,82).

claim: When a phone companion assists a TV-led session, let the phone answer only the TV's open ask by its id and refuse phone requests that navigate or change session state, because the TV must stay the single author of navigation.
because: Study Desk desk refuses phone posts that seat a learner or move the TV (409 otherwise); re-walked 2026-10-22 (STICK-PHONE-REWALK line 55).

claim: When a TV app may ship on a platform that can forbid listening sockets, put the transport behind one interface with both a LAN listener and an outbound relay, both tested, because the relay is the escape hatch.
because: firetv decision 0004; Vega OS docs are silent on inbound sockets (friction-log FL-11).

claim: When a model contributes to a user-facing verdict, decide the verdict in deterministic code and let the model only explain or phrase it, re-checking any solution the model shows, because marks stay testable offline and model failures cannot become wrong verdicts.
because: Study Desk rules suites (102 suites, 2,609 tests) run with models stubbed; Math Buddy withholds a verdict when the model's own solution disagrees with the code's check.

claim: When CI must stay keyless and free, record live model quality on the machine that has the models as committed counts-only drift records and have CI fail on a missing, stale (over 21 days) or alerting record, because otherwise drift is measured only when someone remembers.
because: firetv decision 0014; drift records 2026-10-23-1/-2 at b48c4571 and 5ca59c30 (maths 10/10, essay 4/4, lessons 8/9, no alert).

claim: When a change touches what a model is asked, derive that live surface from the bench's import graph and require the change to carry a fresh live record compared in code against the base's newest, because a weekly drift run catches prompt regressions only after merge.
because: firetv decision 0017; tools/model-drift-pr.cjs --base gated every Study Desk push on 2026-10-23.

claim: When a manifest records verified capabilities, re-prove them on every same-repo PR (never on fork PRs, which would run shell commands) and fail a committed true that did not pass, because an unchecked claim goes stale.
because: firetv decision 0016.

claim: When designing a ten-foot TV screen, keep prose to one caption slot and draw the state (a track with a marker, one label), because text-heavy screens read as a book, not a TV app, from the sofa.
because: Study Desk owner rejected text-heavy screens as a book, not a TV app; later waves cut captions to one line.

claim: When judges or testers must run a server-backed prototype, ship a prebuilt standalone zip with seeded demo users, start scripts that print the exact link and the keys to use, and an audit of the zip contents, because a five-minute no-build start is what a reviewer actually tries.
because: Study Desk v1.1-v1.3: package:portable zip (about 14 MB, 2316 entries audited) with demo learners; the browser TV ignores the mouse, so the start scripts print the keys.

claim: When the device you film on is shared with other agents or sessions, take it only under an atomic-mkdir lock with an owner file, hold it at most a few minutes, wait on a busy lock instead of breaking it, and give the device back where you found it confirmed by the device's own heartbeat, because a capture run otherwise takes over or stops someone else's work.
because: Study Desk film: lock.mjs mkdir plus owner file, 5 min hold, 20 s retry, never broken; stick1.log shows 3 give-backs inside one take with heartbeat 'app in focus: true'.

claim: When capturing with adb screenrecord, record one clip per beat, stop it with SIGINT to its own pid (never pkill), send WAKEUP first, then convert the variable-frame-rate clip to a fixed rate and pad it with its last frame, because screenrecord stops at 180 s, writes frames only on change, and a sleeping display records black and drops keys.
because: Study Desk film capture tooling (stick.mjs --time-limit 180, kill -INT pid, KEYCODE_WAKEUP before takeover).

claim: When syncing device footage with host-driven actions, anchor each beat on the first visible frame change its action causes (frame difference on a small grey thumbnail inside a host-clock prior window) and log the residual, because the device and host share no frame-accurate clock and the host clock alone is off by up to about 1 s.
because: Study Desk film: residuals -317..+282 ms on rehearsal, up to 542-644 ms on stick takes; host clock alone off by up to about 1 s.

claim: When a demo depends on a real device and live models, rehearse the whole scripted walk on a browser stand-in of the TV until every beat is green, then run only the verified beats on the device, because the rehearsal is cheap, repeatable and catches script faults before device time is spent.
because: Study Desk film: 8 browser rehearsals vs 4 stick runs; rehearsals reached 16/16 then 20/20 green before the stick take; stick ran only --only verified beats.

claim: When a scripted beat waits on a live model, open its window on the answer arriving and test that the answer was not already on screen, because model latency varies widely and a fixed timer shows either a frozen wait or an answer that landed off camera.
because: Study Desk film: hint latency 17-64 s; a mustWait check failed a beat whose page read was already on screen (residual 2619 ms).

claim: When a model wait inside a beat is longer than the narration can hold, cut it with a short dissolve from the action to the arrival (a jump beat) rather than showing it or hard-cutting it, because frozen waits read as broken and a hard cut reads as a blink.
because: Study Desk film: 15-25 s pitch waits and 8-12 s turns dropped with a 6-frame dissolve (stick4-adult: 6512 ms of action, arrival 4577 ms after the cut).

claim: When capturing several beats in one device session, record every beat first and transcode and composite afterwards, keeping chained beats in one device hold, because heavy work between beats opens gaps where live answers arrive off camera.
because: Study Desk film: 5-10 s of ffmpeg between beats was exactly where the coaching note and the page read landed off camera.

claim: When concatenating per-beat clips for a timed cut, cut each segment to exactly round(ms*fps/1000) frames, write the take's edge times from that frame count, and re-base inputs to PTS 0 with a hold on their last frame, because ffmpeg -t truncates and drifts against the ms sum, so beats open or close on a neighbour's frame.
because: Study Desk film: -t gave 277 frames for 9258 ms where the kit rounded to 278; windows drifted up to 2 frames at 9 of 15 footage cuts and split layouts flashed an empty bezel.

claim: When reviewing a rendered cut, audit it frame by frame for blinks at every cut from bright footage to a plate and cover them with a short wipe in its own revertible commit, because a few frames of bare background read as a flicker that loudness and format gates never flag.
because: Study Desk film: 8 and 2 frames of bare navy before two plates read as a blink; a 500 ms wipe fixed it while the render gates had passed (-14.04 LUFS).

claim: When the film is narrated, measure the narration first and pace each captured beat to its measured hold, and re-capture (and regenerate music cues whose edges moved) after any script or app change that moves a hold, because footage cut to guessed timings drifts against the voice and music.
because: Study Desk film: app changes forced a phase-3 re-take with lines re-narrated and two cues regenerated; v3 regenerated all three cues.

claim: When narration describes live model output or a device claim, re-read each line against the actual take before the paid voice run and again after the device take, and drop or reshoot any beat whose screen contradicts the story, because an automated check proves a claim sits on footage, not that the footage says it.
because: Study Desk film: the recap beat was dropped because its tile read Not tonight against the story; a lower third was added because a faint meta line could not carry the actual-device claim.

claim: When building device capture tooling, keep the raw per-beat clips and a capture log so the take can be re-cut offline, and give scripted beats a retry for server-reported failures, because cutting fixes can then be proved without the shared device and one transient model failure would otherwise sink a whole device run.
because: Study Desk film: recompose.mjs re-cut takes from raw clips; a run with 2 of 4 beats broken by a model timeout went 4/4 after adding a retry on desk-reported failure.
